methodology.how: TWO entry points onto one table. (a) ENSURE: ensure_graph_contracts_table(catalog) (:197-207) builds table_id = ("globgrph", "graph_contracts") at :202 and calls _ensure_table (:203), which load_table-or-create_table (:112-122, create at :120) against the RATIFIED schema _graph_contracts_schema() (:167). This is reachable from the NIGHTLY (PATH A calls it at :305) and from --ensure-contracts (:2232). It CREATES A TABLE but writes no rows. (b) LOAD: load_contracts_from_yaml() (:1102-1240), reached via --load-contracts (:2238). It normalises YAML rows, skips ids already present unless named in --overwrite (:1163), FAILS CLOSED on an unstampable ratified_at pin (:1204-1206, returns 1 with NOTHING written), then branches: if overwriting, tbl.overwrite(pa_table, overwrite_filter=In("contract_id", ids)) at :1214 -- a SCOPED delete+append in one Nessie commit, rows outside the filter untouched; else tbl.append(pa_table) at :1217, append-only. It then RE-READS the table (:1222) and gates on a per-row integrity check, returning 1 if any row fails (:1233-1236).

declared_opinions: The TO described PATH B as 'APPEND-ONLY (:116...'. MEASURED CORRECTION, and it is a REFINEMENT not a contradiction: append-only is the DEFAULT (:1217) and the skip message at :1163 says so verbatim -- 'already-present (append-only; pass --overwrite to replace)'. But a SCOPED OVERWRITE EXISTS at :1214 behind the --overwrite flag (:2246). So mutation_policy is append_only-by-default with an explicit, id-scoped operator escape -- not append_only absolutely. Carding it as pure append-only would tell a consumer that a contract row can never be replaced in place, which is false.

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: FAILS CLOSED, repeatedly and by design -- this is the most defensive path in the file. Unstampable ratified_at pin -> print ERROR, return 1, NOTHING written (:1204-1206). Post-write integrity gate: re-reads the table (:1222), checks each written row (:1231), and on any failure prints 'ERROR: WRITE_VERIFY_GATE FAILED' and returns 1 (:1233-1236). Already-present id without --overwrite -> SKIPPED with a reason string (:1163), not silently merged.
silent_degrade_paths: The ENSURE half is the exception to this path's fail-closed character, and the asymmetry is worth stating plainly: when reached from the NIGHTLY (:305) a failure is swallowed into 'WARN: GRAPH_CONTRACTS_ENSURE_FAIL' on an rc=0 run (:306-308). That is a deliberate trade -- the comment at :303-304 says a contracts-ensure failure must not fail the nightly graph commit -- but a consumer scoring the nightly on exit code cannot see it.

The WRITE_VERIFY gate re-reads through the SAME catalog client that just wrote (:1222). It is a genuine read-back and it caught the real period_defs-wipe bug, but it shares an instrument with the write: a catalog-layer fault that corrupted both the write and the read-back identically would pass the gate. This is a residual, not an observed defect.
